description: Two ways of asking for an allocation the core cannot perform, and why both have to be refusals rather than approximations. First: an unknown method. `setAllocationScheme` used to read `method`, echo it back in its answer and then ignore it entirely, so asking for anything other than the step ladder returned step-ladder numbers labelled with the name of a different procedure — the worst shape a defect can take, because the reply asserts it did what was asked. It is now E_INPUT_INVALID, and the two the core does perform are named in the message. Second: a scheme with no way out. The simultaneous-equation method solves the whole scheme at once, and a group of cost centres that passes everything among themselves without ever reaching one that keeps it produces a singular system — cost circulates forever, and there is no answer to round to. E_COSTING_UNSOLVABLE names the centre where the elimination ran out, so the modelling mistake is findable. Note the step ladder answers the same shape differently and correctly: for it a cycle is a violation of its own precondition (E_COSTING_CYCLE), while for the equation method a cycle is the ordinary case and only a CLOSED one is fatal.
